channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Relator da indicação de Messias ao STF apresenta parecer favorável e abre caminho a AGU de Lula
item.description: The rapporteur for Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF in the Senate, Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), issued a favorable opinion on the nominee chosen by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, paving the way for AGU approval and advancing the nomination toward Senate hearings.

item.title: Após avisar Motta, Lula envia projeto de fim da escala 6×1 para o Congresso
item.description: Hours after having lunch with House Speaker Hugo Motta, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sent to Congress a bill proposing the end of the 6×1 work schedule. The text is already on the list of proposals under constitutional urgency, which could block the legislative agenda if not voted on within 45 days. The initiative aims to speed up the discussion, either through this bill or the PEC already underway in the Chamber.

item.title: Governo Lula encaminha ao Congresso projeto de lei para o fim da escala 6×1
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has sent to Congress a bill with constitutional urgency to end the 6×1 work schedule and reduce the weekly workweek to 40 hours without salary reduction. The proposal aims to give workers more time for family, leisure, and rest, but faces opposition from the Centrão and other political groups, with a vote expected in late April and skepticism about its approval in May.

item.title: Ministros Nunes Marques e André Mendonça são eleitos presidente e vice do TSE
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) elected Minister Nunes Marques as president and Minister André Mendonça as vice-president on Tuesday, the 14th. The vote was conducted via electronic ballot, resulting in 6 votes to 1 in favor of Nunes Marques, and the newly elected officials will lead the TSE during the 2026 General Elections. Outgoing President Minister Cármen Lúcia emphasized the candidates' experience and the need for continuity in electoral justice ahead of the upcoming vote.

item.title: Motta reclama de Boulos durante encontro com Lula
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta complained to President Lula during a Tuesday meeting about Minister Guilherme Boulos's 'belligerent' stance against the legislature. Motta argued that Boulos lacks support even within his own party, PSOL, and that his actions harm government management.

item.title: Lula tem o dobro de apoio entre idosos do que junto aos mais jovens, aponta Datafolha
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows that President Lula's government approval among seniors (60+) is double that of young adults (16-24): 36% rate it as 'excellent and good' among the elderly, compared to 18% among youth. Nationally, negative perception of the government remains stable at 40%, while Lula's personal disapproval rose to 51%. The survey, conducted April 7-9 with 2,004 respondents, has a 5-point margin of error.

item.title: Em vitória de Lula e Motta, Câmara aprova Odair Cunha para o TCU
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies elected Odair Cunha (PT-MG) as the new minister of the TCU with 303 votes, defeating Elmar Nascimento (União Brasil-BA), who received 96 votes. The vote was secret and involved five candidates, with the PL withdrawing Soraya Santos’ candidacy to rally support behind Elmar Nascimento in an effort to unite opposition to the PT’s nominee. Odair Cunha, a six-term deputy with a reputation for political moderation and articulation, will now have his name forwarded to the Senate as a PDL for final approval.

item.title: TSE suspende julgamento de governador de Roraima com placar de 2 a 1 por cassação
item.description: The TSE has again suspended the trial that could remove Roraima Governor Edilson Damião from office and render former Governor Antonio Denarium ineligible, following a request for vista by Minister Estela Aranha. So far, the vote stands 3-0 in favor of convicting Denarium and 2-1 for removing Damião, with Minister Nunes Marques voting to acquit Damião, citing institutional stability concerns and the risk of having five different governors in a short span. The case stems from allegations of political and economic abuse in the 2022 elections, and a ruling against Damião could trigger supplementary elections in Roraima later this year.

item.title: Relator apresenta parecer favorável à indicação de Messias ao STF
item.description: Senator Weverton (PDT-MA), rapporteur for Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF, issued a favorable opinion, citing constitutional criteria such as impeccable reputation and notable legal expertise. The report emphasizes Messias’ experience at the Attorney General’s Office and his conciliatory profile, concluding there are no technical impediments to approval. The confirmation hearing is scheduled for April 29 in the Senate’s CCJ.

item.title: Senador apresenta relatório favorável a indicação de Messias para o STF
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), rapporteur for Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF, presented a favorable report on Tuesday, to be read in the CCJ on Wednesday and voted in the plenary on the 29th. Messias, current AGU minister, was nominated by Lula last November, facing opposition from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who preferred Rodrigo Pacheco. Despite the initial deadlock, the government secured sufficient support for approval, with both votes being secret and requiring at least 41 favorable votes out of 81 senators.

item.title: “Governo atravessou a rua para proteger ministros”, diz Alessandro Vieira
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), rapporteur of the Organized Crime CPI, accused the federal government of interfering in the final vote on the committee's report, stating that the last-minute inclusion of two PT senators changed the commission's composition and secured the rejection of the document calling for the indictment of three STF ministers and the Attorney General. Vieira argued the change was decisive for the 6-4 vote against the report and maintained that the report's technical content remains valid despite the political outcome.

item.title: TSE volta a suspender julgamento sobre Roraima após voto de Nunes Marques contra novas eleições
item.description: The TSE again suspended the trial on the possible removal of Roraima Governor Edilson Damião after a dissenting vote by Minister Nunes Marques, who supported the ineligibility of former Governor Antonio Denarium but advocated for keeping Damião in office to prevent institutional instability. Marques warned that Damião’s removal could trigger up to five governor changes in six months, undermining governability. He also argued Damião was not directly involved in the alleged misconduct and that the case should not automatically penalize the ticket absent direct impact on election fairness.

item.title: Bancada do PT apresenta projeto que proíbe bets em todo o país
item.description: Pedro Uczai, leader of the PT caucus in the Chamber of Deputies, introduced Bill 1808/2026, proposing a total ban on fixed-odds betting in Brazil, covering both digital and physical operations, advertising, sponsorships, and financial transactions, while repealing existing laws that regulate the sector. Backed by President Lula’s statements, the initiative aims to protect the population from the social, economic, and health impacts of betting, including household debt and strain on the SUS.

item.title: Nunes Marques é o primeiro ministro indicado por Bolsonaro a assumir o TSE
item.description: Kássio Nunes Marques was elected president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on Tuesday night (April 14), becoming the first minister appointed by Jair Bolsonaro to assume the position. He and his vice-president, André Mendonça, are set to take office in the first half of May, following the early departure of Minister Cármen Lúcia. Nunes Marques pledged a more measured, less interventionist approach focused on electoral serenity in 2026, contrasting with the 2022 clashes between Bolsonaro and then-TSE president Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Tarcísio recebe movimento Legendários em São Paulo
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas met with members of the Christian movement Legendários at the Palácio dos Bandeirantes on April 13, 2026, where he delivered a speech citing biblical passages and participated in group rituals. The event included State Deputy Paulo Corrêa Júnior (PSD), who authored the law establishing 'Legendários Day' in the state. The movement, which promotes a 'Jesus model of masculinity,' has grown rapidly in Brazil and globally, with significant social media visibility.

item.title: Em meio a caso Master, CPI do Crime Organizado rejeita relatório por indiciamento de PGR e 3 ministros do STF
item.description: The Senate's Organized Crime CPI rejected the report by Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) that proposed indicting three STF ministers (Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, Gilmar Mendes) and Prosecutor-General Paulo Gonet over alleged misconduct in the Banco Master scandal. The vote was 6 to 4, with government allies working behind the scenes to change the commission's composition to defeat the report. STF ministers condemned the initiative as an attempt to gain electoral dividends and characterized it as abuse of authority, threatening senatorial ineligibility.

item.title: Aécio Neves convida Ciro Gomes a disputar a Presidência pelo PSDB
item.description: PSDB national president Aécio Neves invited Ciro Gomes to run as the party's presidential candidate in the 2026 elections during the opening of the PSDB national meeting in Brasília. Aécio stated that the political landscape remains undefined and that Brazil may need a 'new Real Plan' to update its work, economy, and development sectors, praising Ciro's qualifications and contributions. Ciro, who joined the PSDB in October 2025 and is 68 years old, said he will mature the idea with respect, without setting a deadline, and noted he holds no public office, eliminating the need for disaffiliation to run.

item.title: Lula envia ao Congresso projeto do fim da jornada de trabalho 6 x 1
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has sent to the National Congress a bill to end the work schedule of six days worked for one day off, submitted on Tuesday, April 14, as shown in an extra edition of the Official Gazette. The measure aims to reduce the weekly workload and improve working conditions in the country.

item.title: Lula sanciona o novo Plano Nacional da Educação: 'Brasil não precisa de escola cívico-militar'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed the new National Education Plan (PNE), establishing strategic guidelines for Brazilian education over the next ten years, covering all levels from early childhood to postgraduate education. During the ceremony, Lula emphasized that Brazil does not need civic-military schools, reaffirming the commitment to public, secular, and inclusive education.

item.title: Motta reclama de Boulos a Lula e diz que ele adota tom beligerante
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) criticized Minister Guilherme Boulos (Secretary-General) during lunch with President Lula, stating that Boulos adopts a belligerent tone toward the Legislature. The complaint was made on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, reflecting tensions between the Executive and Congress.

item.title: Relator apresenta parecer favorável à indicação de Jorge Messias para o STF
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha issued a favorable report on Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF, with hearings set for April 29 and a Senate plenary vote the same day. Messias requires at least 41 votes to fill the vacancy left by Luís Roberto Barroso. Although backed by the rapporteur, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre initially advocated for Rodrigo Pacheco and criticized the government’s delay in formally submitting the nomination.

item.title: CPI do Crime Organizado: Relator diz que manobra para rejeitar parecer teve 'intervenção direta' do Palácio do Planalto
item.description: The rapporteur of the Organized Crime CPI, Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), accused the Planalto Palace of directly intervening in the replacement of committee members to secure the rejection of his report, which sought the indictment of three STF ministers and the PGR. The change of three titular members hours before the vote shifted the outcome to 6-4 against the report. Vieira stated that, without the interference, the report would have been approved.

item.title: Lula: ‘A direita diz que Ramagem foi preso por multazinha, mas ele foi condenado por golpe’
item.description: President Lula stated that Alexandre Ramagem, former federal deputy and ex-director of Abin, is convicted of 16 years for attempted coup and armed criminal organization, and that his arrest by ICE in the U.S. should lead to his extradition to serve his sentence in Brazil. He rejected claims from the right, especially Eduardo Bolsonaro, that the arrest was for a minor traffic violation, emphasizing that Ramagem was convicted by the STF and is ineligible for 8 years. Lula expressed belief that Ramagem will return to Brazil to serve his sentence.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes quer ação contra Alessandro Vieira; ala da corte articula inelegibilidade
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes intends to file a criminal complaint against Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) with the Attorney General's Office, in response to the Organized Crime CPI report that sought to indict Supreme Court ministers, including Mendes, Toffoli, and Moraes. The CPI rejected the report by a 6-4 vote after a last-minute change in its composition, with Vieira claiming evidence of responsibility crimes. Behind the scenes, a faction of the STF is exploring legal avenues to render Vieira ineligible for the 2026 elections, arguing that his direct targeting of justices crossed an institutional red line.

item.title: Nunes Marques é eleito presidente do TSE; André Mendonça será vice
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques was elected president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) by seniority, with a two-year term starting at the end of May, succeeding Minister Cármen Lúcia. Minister André Mendonça will serve as vice-president. The election was symbolic and conducted via electronic ballot, following the seniority rule among STF justices who comprise the TSE.

item.title: Nunes Marques é o 1º indicado por Bolsonaro eleito presidente do TSE
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques has been chosen as the next president of the TSE, becoming the first appointee of former President Jair Bolsonaro to lead the court during a presidential election. His appointment marks a historic moment, as no minister previously appointed by Bolsonaro had ever presided over the TSE during an electoral cycle. The decision comes amid rising tensions between the Executive and Judiciary over the conduct of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Impasse trava regulação de trabalho por aplicativo, e Congresso só deve voltar a tratar do tema em 2027
item.description: The regulation of app-mediated work has been postponed until after the 2026 elections, due to the electoral calendar and a lack of consensus on a minimum pay model for drivers and delivery workers. The scheduled vote in the special committee and the Chamber of Deputies plenary this week was canceled, and Congress is not expected to revisit the issue until 2027.

item.title: É falso que Lula pediu para TSE proibir vídeos na internet nas eleições
item.description: It is false that President Lula asked the TSE to ban videos on the internet during the 2026 elections. The government proposed only to prohibit 'video-cut championships' — competitions that pay influencers to spread electoral propaganda through edited and ranked videos — like those promoted by Pablo Marçal in 2024. The measure aims to counterpaid electoral propaganda disguised as viral content, not to restrict freedom of expression or general video sharing.

item.title: Lula diz que o Brasil não precisa de escola cívico-militar na educação
item.description: President Lula signed the National Education Plan (PNE) and stated that Brazil does not need to expand civic-military schools in public education, arguing that all students should follow the same national curriculum. He emphasized that the PNE aims to increase public education investment from 5.5% to 10% of GDP by 2036, with goals to universalize preschool, literacy by the end of 2nd grade, and extend school hours in 50% of public schools by 2031. Lula stressed the need for societal oversight to ensure plan implementation and highlighted the challenge of motivating students to value education.

item.title: Lula envia ao Congresso proposta de redução da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Lula sent a workweek reduction bill (ending the 6x1 scale) to Congress under constitutional urgency after agreeing with Hugo Motta. The proposal modifies the CLT and related labor laws, giving Congress 45 days to vote. If not voted on, it would block the congressional agenda. Motta initially wanted it as a PEC, but Lula chose a bill for symbolic weight, with both tracks now being negotiated jointly by Guimarães, Motta, and government leaders to prioritize one and avoid legislative conflict through 2026-2027.

item.title: Governo derruba relatório da CPI do Crime após troca de senadores
item.description: The Crime Organized CPI rejected the report of rapporteur Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) by a 6-4 vote, following senator changes that strengthened PT and government influence. The report called for the indictment of three STF ministers (Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, Gilmar Mendes) and Attorney General Paulo Gonet over alleged misconduct in the Banco Master case. The replacement of Sérgio Moro and Marcos do Val with PT senators Teresa Leitão and Beto Faro was denounced by Vieira as direct government interference.

item.title: Fachin repudia em nota inclusão de ministros do STF em relatório da CPI do Crime: ‘Indevida’
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Edson Fachin rejected the inclusion of fellow justices and the Prosecutor General in the final report of the Crime Organized CPI, calling it 'inappropriate' and defending the independence of Brazil's Powers. Mendes and Toffoli also criticized the report as electorally motivated, warning its authors could lose their mandates. The report, by Senator Alessandro Vieira, calls for impeachment over the Banco Master case but requires Senate President Davi Alcolumbre's approval to have any effect.

item.title: Nunes Marques é eleito o novo presidente do TSE; André Mendonça é o novo vice-presidente
item.description: Nunes Marques was elected president of the TSE and André Mendonça vice-president, in a protocolary rotation election. Both were nominated to the STF by Jair Bolsonaro and are expected to defend the credibility of electronic voting machines. Nunes Marques replaces Minister Cármen Lúcia as president of the Court.

item.title: Fachin repudia inclusão de ministros do STF em relatório de CPI: ‘Desvio de finalidade’
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin criticized the inclusion of STF ministers in the Organized Crime CPI report, calling it a thematic deviation that weakens democratic pillars and threatens fundamental rights. The commission rejected, by 6 votes to 4, the report by Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) proposing indictments of Gilmar Mendes, Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, and Prosecutor General Paulo Gonet.

item.title: Fachin repudia relatório da CPI do Crime Organizado que mirou ministros do STF
item.description: STF President Edson Fachin emphatically rejected the request to indict Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes by the Organized Crime CPI, stating they were 'unduly mentioned'. He emphasized that while CPIs are a democratic guarantee, thematic deviations weaken democratic pillars and threaten fundamental rights.

item.title: Fabinho faz gol da vitória do Al-Ittihad na prorrogação do duelo com o Al-Wahda, pela Champions Asiática
item.description: Brazilian midfielder Fabinho scored the winning goal in extra time as Al-Ittihad defeated Al-Wahda 1-0 in the Asian Champions League. After a VAR-reviewed penalty was awarded in the 129th minute, Fabinho calmly placed the ball in the center of the goal. His composure under pressure strengthens his case as a backup to Casemiro for Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad.

item.title: Governo usa dispositivo vetado por Lula e retomado pelo Congresso no novo licenciamento para acelerar obra da BR-319
item.description: The Lula government used a provision from the General Environmental Licensing Law, previously vetoed by the president and later reinstated by Congress, to authorize pavement works on the BR-319 highway, the only land link between Manaus and the rest of Brazil. The authorization, supported by an AGU opinion and a DNIT technical note, frames the project as maintenance of existing infrastructure, despite environmentalist warnings about deforestation and pandemic risks. Lula is expected to visit the construction site between the 27th and 28th of this month, amid the 2026 election campaign.

item.title: Fachin repudia proposta de relator de CPI de indiciamento de ministros do STF: 'desvios de finalidade'
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin strongly denounced the proposed indictment of ministers Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes by Senator Alessandro Vieira in the Senate Organized Crime CPI, calling it a 'diversion of purpose' that undermines democratic pillars and threatens fundamental rights. The CPI rejected the report by a 6-4 vote. Fachin stressed the need to uphold the independence of branches of government and constitutional rights, stating no one is above the law.

item.title: Fachin repudia inclusão de ministros do STF em relatório da CPI e fala em ameaça a direitos fundamentais
item.description: Supreme Court President Luiz Edson Fachin denounced the inclusion of Ministers Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes in the final report of the Organized Crime CPI, calling it improper and warning that thematic deviations in parliamentary inquiries threaten fundamental rights and democratic pillars. He emphasized that CPIs are legitimate when constitutionally bounded and reaffirmed the STF’s commitment to upholding the Constitution and democratic freedoms.

item.title: Planalto critica inclusão de ministros do STF em relatório de CPI
item.description: The minister of Institutional Relations, José Guimarães (PT), stated the government will act to defeat the report of the Organized Crime CPI that calls for investigating STF ministers, calling the opinion 'absurd' for not indicting criminal organization members. The statement reinforces the Planalto's strategy to block the report in the vote, aligned with PT leaders like Pedro Uczai and Gleisi Hoffmann, who criticize the commission's shift in focus. The move aims to prevent Congress-Judiciary tensions and test the cohesion of the government base.

item.title: Relatório de Alessandro Vieira que pedia indiciamento dos ministros do STF é rejeitado
item.description: Senators rejected the final report of the Organized Crime CPI, drafted by Senator Alessandro Vieira, which called for the indictment of three Supreme Federal Court ministers — Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes and Gilmar Mendes — and Attorney General Paulo Gonet, for crimes of responsibility. The report was voted down by six senators in favor and four against, leading to its rejection.

item.title: Fim da escala 6×1: Motta garante a Lula consulta a líderes após envio de proposta
item.description: Speaker Hugo Motta assured President Lula that he would consult party leaders on ending the 6x1 work scale if the government submits a bill to reduce the workweek. The meeting aimed to ease tensions and included Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães and Government Leader Paulo Pimenta. Lula intends to send his own bill due to his union background, viewing the current constitutional amendment as too slow.

item.title: CPI do Crime Organizado rejeita relatório que visava impeachment de ministros do STF e PGR
item.description: The Organized Crime CPI rejected, by a vote of 6 to 4, the report by Senator Alessandro Vieira calling for the indictment and possible impeachment of STF Ministers Dias Toffoli, Alexandre de Moraes, Gilmar Mendes, and Attorney General Paulo Gonet. The rejection followed a government-led maneuver to alter the committee’s composition and secure a majority opposed to the report, after pressure from the targeted ministers. Vieira claimed he had been threatened by STF justices, while CPI President Fabiano Contarato stated there is no evidence of intentional wrongdoing to justify indictment.

item.title: CPI rejeita relatório que atingia ministros do STF após articulação de governo e tribunal
item.description: The Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) on Organized Crime rejected, by a 6-4 vote, a report proposing the indictment of Supreme Court Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, and Gilmar Mendes. The decision came after coordination between the federal government and the STF itself, which acted to block the investigation’s progress. The outcome reflects institutional resistance to investigations targeting members of the Supreme Court.

item.title: Ministro do Turismo apresenta a países vizinhos medida que zera impostos sobre querosene de aviação
item.description: Tourism Minister Gustavo Feliciano presented to neighboring countries a temporary tax exemption on aviation kerosene (QAV) to curb fuel price increases driven by the Middle East war. The measure was discussed at the World Travel Market Latin America 2026 in São Paulo, where Feliciano said regional partners showed interest in cooperation. QAV is essential for 30% of Brazil’s turboprop fleet and rose 51.6% in price during the study period.

item.title: CPI do Crime Organizado enterra parecer de relator que mirava Moraes, Gilmar e Toffoli
item.description: The Organized Crime CPI defeated the final report by Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), which proposed the indictment of Supreme Court ministers and the Attorney General, after a government-backed maneuver replaced two opposition senators with government allies. The vote ended 6 against and 4 in favor, blocking approval of the report. The last-minute change in the committee’s composition shifted the balance of power and led to the political demise of the report.

item.title: Acordo econômico com Canadá sai em 2026, diz ministro
item.description: Marcio Elias Rosa, Brazil's Minister of Development, Industry, Trade and Services, stated that the Mercosul-Canada trade agreement is expected to be signed in 2026, with over half the text already negotiated. Talks with the United Arab Emirates have stalled and are unlikely to conclude this year. He also confirmed the provisional application of the Mercosul-European Union agreement starting May 1, 2026, which will eliminate tariffs on 95% of NCMs in the EU immediately, while advocating for greater protection of Brazilian industry within the bloc.

item.title: Se Caiado ou qualquer governador precisar de recursos, não tem como não atender, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated he does not treat governors based on partisanship and will support any governor who has a valid reason and feasible projects, citing Ronaldo Caiado as an example of an opposition figure who could still receive federal aid if his demands are justified.

item.title: Incentivo fiscal para data centers é prioritário, diz ministro
item.description: Minister of Development, Industry, Commerce and Services Márcio Elias Rosa stated that the Lula government will prioritize fiscal incentives for data centers, aiming to approve Bill 278/2026 establishing the Redata regime after the provisional measure expired. He emphasized dialogue with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to advance the initiative, noting the incentives aim to suspend federal taxes such as PIS/Cofins and IPI on equipment purchases for data processing centers.

item.title: Lula acerta com Motta envio de projeto para o fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: President Lula and Chamber Speaker Hugo Motta agreed to send a bill to end the 6x1 work schedule after a lunch at the Planalto Palace. The bill will be processed under constitutional urgency, while the related PEC will continue its scheduled review in the Chamber’s CCJ. The negotiation, led by new Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães, aims to prevent conflicts between the two proposals by prioritizing a simple, streamlined text to ease congressional approval.
